answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a unique copper ingot weighed and stamped only at a designated harbor jetty. An attacker forging 800 aliases must source and ship 800 separate ingots through real docks for inspection, costing more metal and logistics than any reward recovers. Honest agents reuse one verified sample across epochs while the public ledger of jetty stamps exposes bulk forgeries. The mechanism forces the farm to pay linear physical costs that cannot be pooled.
